claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was a Christian theologian who lived circa 185–254 CE, was born in Alexandria, Egypt and died in Tyre, Phoenicia.
He served as head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria and was later ordained a priest, eventually founding the Christian school at Caesarea.
Origen composed extensive biblical commentaries on most of the Pauline letters, including a commentary on the Epistle to the Ephesians.
The original commentary does not survive in full; only short passages survive in a Byzantine catena and are quoted by Jerome in his own commentary on Ephesians.
The surviving fragments were first published in modern critical editions in the early twentieth century, notably in the Journal of Theological Studies (1901‑1902).
